title: Tell no one (Matthew 17:1–13)
hookLine: a voice that stops mid-song, and three friends face down on a mountain
tomorrow: why would Jesus pay a tax with a coin from a fish's mouth?

cards: It happens at recitals, in job interviews, in the middle of a toast: halfway through, the voice just stops, and the room goes very quiet. Three friends on a mountain are in their own version of that moment.
Peter, James and John are face down on the ground, too frightened to look up. Minutes ago Jesus' face was shining. Moses and Elias were there, talking with him.
Peter, never quiet for long, offered to build something. Then a bright cloud, and a voice out of it. Now nobody is talking.
What happens next is very small.

teach.h: HIS FACE DID SHINE AS THE SUN.
teach.b: Go back up the mountain a few minutes. Matthew says he was transfigured before them: "his face did shine as the sun, and his raiment was white as the light." Elias is the King James name for Elijah.

Peter answers the way people do when something is too big to hold: "Lord, it is good for us to be here," and he offers to put up tabernacles, little shelters, one each. He's still talking when the cloud comes.
The voice says, "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him." Not build for him. Hear him.
And they fall on their faces. Here is the answer to the silence. No thunder.

"Jesus came and touched them, and said, Arise, and be not afraid." When they look up, the shining is gone, and there's only Jesus, their friend, standing there. The hand comes first; the explanations come later.

teach.h: TELL THE VISION TO NO MAN.
teach.b: Then, on the way down, an odd order: "Tell the vision to no man, until the Son of man be risen again from the dead."
Keep it quiet, for now. So they carry two things down the mountain: a touch that got them off the ground, and a secret with a date on it.

how: Some churches keep a feast of the Transfiguration and read this story aloud on it, and some Christians hold on to the words arise, and be not afraid in frightening times.

o: a rule that every prayer must stay secret
an order to keep the vision quiet for now
a warning never to speak of God in public

s: Jesus told the three to tell everyone what they saw
he charged them: tell the vision to no man, until the Son of man be risen again from the dead.
Peter offered to build shelters on the mountain
Lord, it is good for us to be here: he offered three tabernacles, one each for Jesus, Moses and Elias.
tell no one meant keep it secret forever
the order has an end date: until the Son of man be risen again from the dead.

games.q: your little brother wakes from a nightmare, shaking, and asks what it meant. you could explain dreams, or do something else first. what comes first in Matthew 17?
o: a hand on his shoulder, and: it's okay, get up, you're safe.
a careful explanation, so he understands what the dream was.
tell him to keep it to himself so it doesn't scare anyone.
games.why: after the cloud, Jesus came and touched them and said, Arise, and be not afraid. the touch came before any explanation.

practice: Rest one hand on your own shoulder or forearm, the way you'd steady a friend, and let it stay there, warm and still, while you breathe.
If someone you love is near, a hand on their shoulder for a moment, no words, does the same thing. Let the touch come first, before any explaining.

wordCard.voice: Tell no one. The order on the way down: keep the vision quiet until the Son of man is risen from the dead.

orig.note: Greek: he was transfigured, Matthew's word for what happened before them in 17:2.

carryVoice: Your line: arise, be not afraid. The hand came before the explanation. See you tomorrow.
